The present Dar arises out of road accident in which one Rohan Das, aged about 7 years, suffered injuries. In terms of the provision of Motor Vehicle Act, the same is treated as a claim petition. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 07.11.2021, upon receipt of information through Dd no. 41A regarding flipping of a vehicle near Khanna Market, Lodhi Road, investigating officer reached the Rohan Das (Dar) vs Akendra Kumar(206/21,Lc) on 21 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190590054/ 1 spot where one vehicle Eicher Tempo bearing no. texts.facts: In response to the Dar, insurance company filed its reply denying its liability to compensate the petitioner on the ground that the offending vehicle was being plied in violation of the permit as per which the offending vehicle was only allowed to be use as a light goods carriage vehicle.
texts.arguments: It has been argued on behalf of the petitioners that since that son of petitioner no.1 lost his life in the accident that is proved to have occurred due to rash and negligent driving by respondent no.1, Rohan Das (Dar) vs Akendra Kumar(206/21,Lc) on 21 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190590054/ 3 respondent no.3, with which the offending vehicle was insured may be directed to compensate the petitioners. On the other hand, it is argued by respondent no.1 Digitally signed by CHARU CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2024.10.21 MACT No. 325/22 Rohan Das vs. Akendra & 0rs. Page no. 5 of 04:20:43 24(ss)+0530 and 2 that the petitioners have failed to prove rash and negligent driving by respondent no.1 or the involvement of the vehicle in the alleged accident. It is further argued that even if the accident is assumed to be proved, it is respondent no.3 which is liable to compensate the petitioners. It is argued on behalf of respondent no.3 that the petitioner/victims were traveling in the offending vehicle as unauthorized and gratuitous passengers since the offending vehicle was a goods carriage vehicle. It is argued that the offending vehicle was insured as a goods carriage vehicle and could not carry any passenger except for the driver and owner of the goods. It is further argued that the insured i.e. respondent no.2 has further violated the condition of RC which permitted a maximum of 3 persons to be seated in the offending vehicle. It is argued that as there is a clear breach of the terms and condition of the insurance policy, insurance company is not liable to compensate the victims.
